title: Germany – Railway construction works – Rahmenvereinbarung für Instandsetzungsleistungen im konstruktiven Ingenieurbau
description: Rahmenvereinbarung konstruktiver Ingenieurbau für Instandsetzungsleistungen, 6 Raumlose (Mitte, Nord, Süd, Südost, Südwest, West), 1 bis 7 Gewerkelose je Raumlos - Mögliche Gewerkelose in den Raumlosen: Massivbau, Tiefbau, Stahlbau, Gerüstbau, Felssicherung, Korrosionsschutz, Betoninstandsetzung. Die maximale Anzahl der je Gewerkelos vorgesehenen zu bindenden Rahmenvertragspartner (Auftragnehmer) sind in der Anlage 01.01 Wichtige Informationen enthalten. Bei den in den LVen der Gewerkelose abgebildeten Mengen (Warenkorb) handelt es sich ausschließlich um kalkulatorische sowie für die Angebotswertung relevante Angaben. Ein Anspruch auf Beauftragung der Gesamtmengen besteht nicht. In den Gewerkelosen wird über die Vertragslaufzeit eine Preisgleitformel (Material, Lohn, Energie sowie fester Kostenanteil) entsprechend den Regelungen in der Anlage 2.28 vereinbart. Der Bieter kann je Gewerkelos einen Staffelnachlass für jeden Einzelauftrag anbieten. Der Staffelnachlass wird im Rahmen der Wertung zu einem Wertungsnachlass zusammengezogen. Die festgelegten Staffeln und Gewichtungen sind in Anlage 2.25 festgelegt. Es wird darauf hingewiesen, dass die vertraglich geregelte Verfahrensweise der möglichen Preisgleitung Auswirkungen auf den Preiswettbewerb haben können, der bei Vergabe der Einzelverträge durchzuführen ist. Einzelheiten hierzu sind der Anlage 2.28.2 (Preisgleitklausel), dort Ziff. 7, zu entnehmen. Die Hauptvertragslaufzeit der Rahmenvereinbarung ist von 04.05.2027-31.12.2030. Die Rahmenvereinbarung hat je Gewerkelos in den Raumlosen unterschiedliche Einzelvertragsabrufhöhen entsprechend §2 Absatz 2.1 der Rahmenvereinbarung und siehe Einzellosbeschreibungen im Bekanntmachungstext.

description: Účelem veřejné zakázky je uzavření smlouvy s jedním (1) dodavatelem na realizaci předmětu veřejné zakázky. Předmětem plnění veřejné zakázky je provedení stavebních prací spočívajících v elektrifikaci autobusové linky č. 131 v trase Bořislavka - Hradčanská. Předmět plnění (stavba) zahrnuje instalaci trolejového vedení na vybraných úsecích trasy autobusové linky, včetně napájecích kabelů a potřebné technologie. title: PHASE A SAMPLING THE NEUTRAL DENSITY OF THE LOWER THERMOSPHERE - EXPRO+
description: Objectives and TasksThe activity aims to reach a preliminary design for a dedicated mission that will measure in-situ the neutral density, and when feasible the ion density as well, in very low-Earth orbit, i.e. the lower thermosphere below 250km and if feasiblebelow 200km, from aneccentric orbit with high inclination. The eccentricity shall be tuned to ensure orbital lifetimes spanning a significant part of the solar cycle and the high inclination shall ensure the capture of samples across the dynamic atmospheric regions that affect the majority of current spacecraft and can support the new generation of VLEO satellites.To couple in-situ measurements that can be used to calibrate atmosphere models in the region of interest with space safety applications such as improved orbital lifetime estimation of collision avoidance risk assessment, direct coupling with the mission dragprofiles is needed. Therefore, the mission shall embark an accelerometer and optimise its shape and AOCS control to facilitate precise orbit determination.Very low perigee orbits, with apogee still in low Earth orbit, are a challenge for space surveillance and tracking systems due to limited visibility from individual sensors and the orbit being highly affected by drag. The mission shall function as a calibration target for commercial tracking solution in Europe, to demonstrate the accuracy of their products against a ground truth provide by the mission in support of safely operating in the VLEO regime.To prepare for the above-described mission, the proposed activity will assess the overall feasibility of the mission and specifically include: Mission and requirements definition: redefine in detail the purpose and mission objectives deriving consistently the satellite system, the orbital, and the groundsegment requirements. These shall be derived from the identified need of performing orbital lifetime calculation and collision avoidance processes below 300km. Conceptual design: based on the mission definition and system requirements, a conceptual design of the satellite will be developed. This includes the basiclayout of the satellite, the platform mass and size, the orbit, the major components and subsystems considering as well launch vehicle, and groundsegment. Definition of the payload (e.g. mass spectrometers, accelerometers). Identify all critical items (< TRL 6) and derive technology development plans for each including definition of the VV approach. Given the eccentric orbit crossing highly utilised space traffic reason, perform a trade-off in platform manoeuvrability needs to extend the mission duration while managing collusion risk in accordance with ESA's space debris mitigation requirements. Preliminary cost and schedule: estimate of costs and schedules is developed based on the conceptual design, and the system requirements to be below 25MEUR. Risk assessment: risks associated with the mission and satellite design will be identified, evaluated, and assessed. Feasibility analysis: the feasibility of the mission and satellite design is assessed, taking into account technical, cost, and schedule considerations. Analysis of the commercialisation opportunities related to the mission concept and the related technologies.

title: Q/V BAND PHASED ARRAY ANTENNA FOR AERONAUTICAL APPLICATIONS (ARTES AT 7A.079) - EXPRO+
description: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture, and test a Q/V band phased array antenna demonstrator for aeronautical applications, including the antenna radiating elements and the main passive components of the beamforming network.Targeted Improvements: - At least twice the number of beams and 3 to 4 times more compact volume compared to Q/V band mechanically scanning antennas.- 2 to 3 times reduced volume compared to Ka band antennas.Description:Today, terminal antennas are mainly exploiting Ka and Ku frequency bands. However, a growing number of satellite operators show interest in the emerging Q/V frequency band both for Geostationary Equatorial Orbit (GEO) and for Non-Geostationary Satellite Orbits (NGSOs). This includes new concepts envisaging service links to base stations and backhaul in Ka as well as in Q/V band. Required components and beamforming networks (BFNs) are increasingly becoming available, especially at Q-band, but these neither address the specific requirements of the satcom market nor cover the higherV-band range. For aeronautical applications, in particular, the Q/V band may enable improved performance (in terms of bandwidth, volume), while still maintaining acceptable link budgets with LEO/GEO satellites.In this activity, a Q/V band phased array antenna for aeronautical applications, suitable for GEO or NGSO satellites shall be developed. The demonstrator shall include antenna radiating elements and the main passive components of the BFN. Active commercial off the self (COTS) components will be included in the final demonstrator. Innovative solutions like those based on multilayer technology will be considered. A trade-off between two solutionswill be performed: one with an antenna aperture combining both transmit and receive functionalities, and one with two separate antenna apertures for the transmission and reception. A single circular polarisation in transmit and a single orthogonal circular polarisation in receive mode can be considered. The antenna demonstrator will be capable of generating two simultaneous beams (minimum target 1 beam). Scanning capabilities between -55 and + 55 degrees in every azimuthal plane shall be guaranteed. A Q/V band demonstrator including 8x8 radiating elements and customised passive BFN to generate two simultaneous beams shall be manufactured (separate Q and V band apertures or a single combined aperture) and tested. Active COTS components will be included in the final demonstrator toguarantee integrability with passive components and to improve the demonstrator representativeness

title: EXPLOITING THE SYNERGY BETWEEN GROUND- AND SPACE-BASED RF MONITORING SYSTEMS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 3A.222) EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: Objective:The objective of the activity is to define, implement, and verify key scenarios that demonstrate the added value of a system integrating both ground- and space-based RF monitoring capabilities.Targeted Improvements:The following figures intend to depict the targeted improvement of a joint ground- and space-based system with respect to an individual ground- or space-based system:Increased detectionaccuracy of at least 20%. Enhanced geolocation precision of at least 15%. Expanded geographical coverage of at least 40%. Reduced response time of at least 30%.Description:While advancements in space-based monitoring technologies have been made, their integration with ground-based systems has not yet been fully realised. Previous efforts have concentrated primarily on enhancing the individual capabilities of either ground or space monitoring, often overlooking the potential benefits that can arise from a collaborative approach.Within Europe, there is an industrial base which offers ground-based interference detection solutions. This activity aims to support this industrial base by developing and validating the techniques to integrate space- and ground-based RF monitoring solutions. The maturity of solutions exploiting space- and ground-monitoring is currently low in Europe. It is foreseen thatthe activity will be supported by existing ground-based infrastructure provided by private parties or national regulators.This activity focuses on the definition, implementation, and demonstration of key scenarios to exploit the potential synergies of ground-based and existing space-based RF monitoring capabilities. These scenarios shall cover various domains, including but not limited to spectrum occupancy, geolocation accuracy, and interference detection, which shall be developed and verified in a representative environment. This involves the reproduction of RF interference conditions to demonstrate the added value of a joint ground and space RF monitoring system and using existing ground- and space-based RF monitoring systems. Additionally, the activity aims to establish operational concepts, including the definition of protocols and security aspectsfor data sharing, operational workflows, and collaborative methodologies that enable the two systems to complement one another effectively.

description: Im Rahmen der Gemeinsamen Europäischen Agrarpolitik sind die europäischen Zahlstellen verpflichtet jährlich eine Qualitätsbewertung für die drei Systeme (LPIS, GSA, AMS) des Integrierten Verwaltungs- und Kontrollsystems (InVeKoS) nach Art. 68, 69 u 70 der VO (EU) 2021/2116 durchzuführen. Hierfür stellt die europäische Kommission (EU-KOM) jährlich VHR-Bilddaten (ohne Orthorektifizierung) des aktuellen Jahres zum Nachvollzug der Überprüfung von Fördervoraussetzungen und Parzellenabgrenzung (Messung) im System zur Identifizierung landwirtschaftlicher Parzellen LPIS (Land Parcel Identification System), geodatenbasierte Antragssystem GSA (Geo-Spatial Application) und dem Flächenüberwachungssystem AMS (Area Monitoring System) bereit. Die VHR-Daten werden über das Kontrolljahr hinweg, je nach Aufnahmemöglichkeit, verteilt durch das JRC (Joint Research Centre) bereitgestellt. Der Aufnahmezeitraum beginnt im März und kann bis in den August hineingehen. Sie sind in Zonen zu je 10 x 10 km über einen bereitgestellten ftp-Link abrufbar. Im Zuge dessen soll die Dienstleistung der Bilddatenaufbereitung für die 6 Zahlstellen der Bundesländer Baden-Württemberg, Bayern, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Rheinland-Pfalz, Schleswig-Holstein und Sachsen über einen Rahmenvertrag zum Abruf bereitgestellt werden. Die Leistung ist ein fertig prozessiertes Bild, dass zum Abruf bereitgestellt wird. Die Zonen werden durch die EU-KOM ausgewählt und in Deutschland auf die einzelnen Bundesländer verteilt. Die Dienstleistung umfasst die Aufbereitung der von der EU_KOM bereitgestellten Satellitendaten (VHR-Daten) im Rahmen der Qualitätsbewertungen der Systeme AMS, GSA und LPIS.
